newsitem.title: UK: Outlook for E.Europe 1996/97 beet crop bleak - Man.
newsitem.headline: Outlook for E.Europe 1996/97 beet crop bleak - Man.

text.p: Prospects for eastern Europe's 1996/97 beet crop are looking bleak with lower production in Ukraine and Russia expected to account for the sharp fall in the region's final sugar output, E D & F Man said on Thursday.
In its first estimate of this season's world sugar balance, Man said eastern European production would fall by 481,000 tonnes to 9.21 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97.
Ukraine and Russia, the region's two largest beet sugar producers, were both forecast to post lower outturns, it said.
Ukraine's 1996/97 sugar output was pegged at 3.15 million tonnes after a previous 3.80 million, and Russian production was expected to fall by 339,000 tonnes to 1.90 million.

Man said Ukraine's white sugar surplus would dwindle to just 900,000 tonnes, white value, and traditional supply arrangements to Russia and other CIS countries would not be met unless Ukraine imported substantial amounts of raw sugar for tolling.

But Ukraine could be discouraged from importing by Russia's moves to protect its own industry through a 10 percent value added tax on Ukrainian imports and talk of introducing an import quota of one million tonnes.
"The net regional increase in import demand would then be felt more in Russia than in Ukraine," it said.
Russia's net sugar deficit was estimated at 3.3 million tonnes for 1996/97 in white value terms, Man said.
Both countries continued to suffer from a lack of herbicides and were having to use old farm equipment.
Extreme weather conditions, such as freezing cold followed by drought and heavy rain, were also responsible for the poorer expected production.
Rains had slowed the start of the harvest and early yields did not look promising, Man said.
